lines.arrive: A room in black and white. You have never been outside it.
lines.scientist: You're a scientist. You know everything there is to know about colour: the light, the eye, the brain. Every physical fact.
lines.tomato: A ripe tomato, on a black and white screen. You know exactly what happens in someone's brain when they see one.
lines.books_1: Light at about seven hundred nanometres. The long-wave cones in the eye fire, and the signal runs to the back of the brain. You know every step.
lines.books_2: What people say when they see it: red. Warm. Like a stop sign. You've read every word they've ever written.
lines.board: The whole spectrum, drawn in chalk. In shades of grey.
lines.desk_early: Not yet. There's still more to read. There always is.
lines.ask: When you step outside and see red for the first time, will you learn anything new?
lines.banana: A blue banana. Someone's idea of a trick. Would all your books have told you that it's blue?
lines.learn_1: So that's what red is like.
lines.learn_2: You knew every fact about seeing red. And still, this is new. Is it a new fact? Or only a new way of knowing an old one?
lines.stay_1: You close the door, and go back to your books.
lines.stay_2: You know everything there is to know about red. Maybe that's all there is to it. Maybe not.
